title: Plan AY: From Vibe Prototype to Viable Product — Pre-Launch Polish Checklist
summary: Lock down requirements → make it testable → error handling → performance → maintainability → documentation
scenario: For the stage of polishing a working prototype into a shippable product, covering robustness and delivery quality — so it doesn't run locally but break in production.

steps.title: Lock down requirements & acceptance criteria
steps.detail: Define what 'it works' means as verifiable acceptance criteria: the core paths, edge behaviors, and what must be handled versus deferred — so polishing doesn't go off the rails. Write out 'when X happens, then Y' cases as the bar for every round of changes.
steps.tips: A 'not in scope' list matters just as much; bounding the scope is how you keep effort on the critical paths.

steps.title: Make the code testable
steps.detail: Add unit tests for critical logic and end-to-end tests for critical paths, so later changes stay regression-safe. Start with the logic most likely to break (data handling, state transitions, external dependencies), then cover the core user flows.
steps.tips: Drive real user paths with Playwright instead of clicking ten times by hand; make the suite reliably green before chasing coverage.

steps.title: Error handling & edge cases
steps.detail: Handle empty states, failure states and invalid inputs one by one so you never show a blank screen or crash; write error messages for the user, not raw stack traces. Timeouts, abnormal API responses and missing data — things that never happen in 'normal' runs — are the most common failure points in production.
steps.tips: Use Playwright to simulate offline, slow responses and empty data to reproduce failure states; every error path needs a visible fallback message.

steps.title: Performance & experience
steps.detail: Use the DevTools Performance and Network panels to find load, interaction and response-time bottlenecks; optimize the slow parts first and avoid over-optimizing. Usually 80% of the gain comes from a few spots: big first-screen requests, uncached resources and render blocking.
steps.tips: Measure before you act and record before/after numbers; set a 'good enough' target (e.g. first screen under 3 seconds) and stop once you hit it.

steps.title: Maintainability
steps.detail: Unify naming, split oversized functions and files, add types and delete dead code so the project can be handed to someone else — or to you in three months. The temporary hacks and hardcoding from the vibe-coding phase get settled back into place here.
steps.tips: Have the AI do a 'readability pass' and confirm each change; keep commits small so everything stays reversible.

steps.title: Documentation & handoff notes
steps.detail: Write down how to run it, environment variables, deployment steps, known issues and limitations — a README or handoff doc anyone can follow. Don't expect someone (or future you) to guess the startup command and prerequisites from the code.
steps.tips: Run the full 'clone to launch' sequence once and record it; every command that appears in the docs must actually work.

pitfalls.title: Treating a working prototype as done
pitfalls.detail: Running locally and staying up in production are different things: caching, concurrency, permissions and weak networks will trip you immediately. Walk through all six steps of this plan before launch.

pitfalls.title: Polishing without tests
pitfalls.detail: Changes verified only by hand fix one thing while breaking another, with regressions caught by eye; automate tests at least for the critical paths so changes stay regression-safe.

pitfalls.title: Ignoring performance & edge cases
pitfalls.detail: Testing only the happy path leaves empty data, failure states and slow networks all uncovered — and production will find them. Treat edge cases as first-class citizens, not afterthoughts.

pitfalls.title: No documentation, no handoff
pitfalls.detail: If only you understand the code, the project goes dark when you leave or take time off; run and deployment notes are the cheapest way to keep it alive.
